title: Telemetry ledger enrichment & historical backfill orchestrator for late-arrival token lineage
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: we continue to see periodic billing discrepancies caused by late-arriving telemetry (edge proxies/region failovers) that lack reconstructed session/session-prefix mappings. These late events land outside the original ingest window and are currently dropped or assigned to fallback buckets, which inflates per-request costs for some tenants and generates noise in chargeback reports.

Goal: implement an idempotent, auditable backfill orchestration service that can: (1) find late telemetry batches, (2) reconstruct token-level lineage and session stitching using existing heuristics + new fingerprinting, (3) write enrichment deltas to the canonical ledger and a verification stream, and (4) surface progress+metrics to Console so finance and SRE can validate corrections.

Design summary:
- Orchestrator service coordinates backfill jobs per-tenant and per-time-window. Jobs are windowed (configurable: 1h/6h/24h), checkpointed, and retryable.
- Worker pipeline implemented as a Beam job (portable runner) consuming from the raw-events bucket + historical Kafka topic; it applies deterministic session-stitching logic, replays KV-cache suffixes where available, and emits enrichment events to a write-ahead verification topic.
- Idempotency: each enrichment record contains a deterministic id (hash of event ids + tenant + window). The ledger writer performs upserts with sequence checks and provides a compensation transaction if a sequence gap is detected.
- Validation: verification stream is consumed by a validator that compares before/after token counts, cost deltas, and candidate conflicting attributions. A summary report is pushed to Console and to a Google Sheet for quick finance review during early rollout.
- Cost control: backfills are rate-limited by tenant with global concurrency caps; heavy tenants require approval/quotas. Backfill jobs have an economic cap to avoid runaway compute cost.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full re-ingest of raw archives would be simplest but compute-prohibitive for large customers. We opt for targeted windowed reprocessing using event-level signature matching to limit rework.
- Use Beam for portability vs Flink for lower-latency streaming; chosen Beam because existing runner compatibility with our batch/kafka hybrid workloads reduces engineering churn.

Observability and audits: all backfill steps emit structured tracing events and an audit record is written per tenant job. Console will show per-job token deltas, estimated dollar impact, and a before/after ledger diff link.

Open questions: can we reuse the existing ledger compaction API or do we need a dedicated transactional writer? How to reconcile multi-region partial replays without double-credits?

acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can process a 72h window for a single tenant end-to-end without duplicate ledger credits
Console displays per-job token delta + estimated dollar impact
Backfill jobs enforce per-tenant rate limits and global concurrency caps
Verification stream and validator produce human-readable diff and attach to job audit record
Finance signs off on a 7-day canary run producing expected reconciliations
